errors.english: because both are subject to error
errors.why: 'khrul ba here is logical deviation (vyabhicāra): blue and utpala each occur without the other, so the words are not co-extensive; it is not 'error'.

note: A generally sound rendering of a difficult grammatical-logical passage on generic and collective words; the deviation (vyabhicāra) terminology is rendered loosely.

span_why: The opening sentence (the person with impaired vision seeing a double moon on opening the eyes, without depending on memory) translates the previous side's last line, not this side.

errors.english: This is prevented by the phrase "free from error" (rab rib med pa) literally: without cataracts/blurriness.
errors.why: The Tibetan cites Dignāga's phrase rab rib bcas, 'with timira' (sataimira), which names the non-conceptual pseudo-perception; there is no 'free from error' / rab rib med pa here.

fix.find: This is prevented by the phrase "free from error" (rab rib med pa) literally: without cataracts/blurriness.
fix.replace: This is excluded by the phrase that teaches "with timira" (rab rib bcas), i.e. affected by eye disease.

errors.english: "possessed of error"
errors.why: rab rib bcas is 'with timira' (sataimira), the eye-disease category of non-conceptual pseudo-perception, not 'possessed of error'.

errors.english: it would not be logical to make the specific distinction here that the fourth type [note: mental perception] is distinct
errors.why: The Tibetan says a misunderstanding (log par rtogs pa) of the phrase 'here the fourth is specially distinguished' would not be reasonable; the English drops the misunderstanding and makes the distinction itself illogical.

errors.english: it would not appear clearly, as is seen with the cognition of a second moon and so forth
errors.why: The subject is the double-moon cognition: it would then not appear vividly as [in] seeing; the English makes it the comparandum instead.

note: The argument is followed, but the key Dignāgan term rab rib bcas (sataimira) is rendered wrongly twice, and the side's opening is preceded by material from the previous side.

errors.english: These arise from the nature of the path, definitive deliverance, and the accomplishment of reasoning.
errors.why: These are the four aspects of the path truth, mārga, nairyāṇika, nyāya (rigs pa) and pratipatti (sgrub pa); the English merges the last two into one and lists three.

fix.find: These arise from the nature of the path, definitive deliverance, and the accomplishment of reasoning.
fix.replace: These arise from the nature of path, deliverance, method and accomplishment.

errors.english: The following are described as the higher factors: mindfulness, the wisdom of discriminating phenomena, and diligence.
errors.why: gong du brjod means these three awakening factors were described above (earlier), not that they are 'higher factors'.

fix.find: The following are described as the higher factors: mindfulness, the wisdom of discriminating phenomena, and diligence.
fix.replace: Mindfulness, the wisdom of discriminating phenomena, and diligence were described above.

errors.english: One then sees the reality that the essence of all beings is non-existent, clear and like a reflection.
errors.why: The whole side is verse (seven-syllable lines) and the English renders it throughout as continuous prose.

note: Follows the enumeration of afflictions abandoned on the path of seeing correctly, but mis-segments the four aspects of the path truth, misreads 'described above', and prosifies the verse.

errors.english: a famine lasting for a year, a month, and seven days
errors.why: bdun ... rnams governs all three units: the famine lasts seven years, seven months and seven days (as in the Abhidharmakośabhāṣya).

fix.find: a famine lasting for a year, a month, and seven days
fix.replace: a famine lasting seven years, seven months, and seven days

errors.english: They search through houses with the tips of sticks for any small scraps of food.
errors.why: This is the 'tally-stick' famine (śalākā): households ration out provisions by sticks ('today the master eats, tomorrow the mistress'), not a search for scraps.

errors.english: The destruction of the world lasts for twenty intermediate aeons.
errors.why: After the destruction (1 + 19 antarakalpas), the destroyed world remains (empty) for twenty; the English conflates this period with the destruction.

errors.english: This is the nature of the five aggregates during the Fortunate Aeon (Bhadrakalpa) and others.
errors.why: The point is that great aeons such as the Bhadrakalpa are themselves of the nature of the five aggregates, not that aggregates have a nature during them.

note: A readable rendering of the Kośa cosmology of the intermediate aeons, with one numerical error in the famine's duration and a few loose readings.

errors.english: such as continuous property and the like
errors.why: rgyun here is most likely a water-stream/channel (property such as water), echoing 'stealing by a stream from the source', not 'continuous property'.

errors.english: it implies that the act was not done according to one's own desire
errors.why: The remark concerns the commentator's arrangement (the topics are summarised by what follows, so it is not arbitrary), not the thief's act.

note: Sound rendering of the Vinaya discussion of owners and stolen requisites; pārājika treatment and the 'by force' clause are correct.

errors.english: Here, in order to find fault with the claim that positive and negative pervasions are not established, the opponent argues:
errors.why: The opponent's objection is that anvaya and vyatireka are NOT established; the English has him attacking that claim.

fix.find: in order to find fault with the claim that positive and negative pervasions are not established, the opponent argues
fix.replace: in order to find fault by claiming that the positive and negative pervasions are not established, the opponent argues

errors.english: the presence of the reason where the predicate exists
errors.why: Anvaya is the presence of the predicate wherever the reason is present; the gloss inverts it.

fix.find: the presence of the reason where the predicate exists
fix.replace: the presence of the predicate wherever the reason is present

errors.english: those things that do not depend on anything else are certain to exist
errors.why: The formal argument says: whatever is independent with respect to X is certain to have X (as the final causal complex is with respect to producing its effect); not that independent things are certain to exist.

errors.english: A functional thing (bhavat)
errors.why: dngos po is bhāva; 'bhavat' is not the term.

note: The momentariness argument is followed well, but the opponent's objection is inverted at one point and the anvaya gloss is backwards.

errors.english: "I know what I do not know" or "I see what I do not see," and speaks with vanity and falsehood
errors.why: This is her later confession to the nuns: 'Ladies, not knowing, I said I know; not seeing, I said I see; I spoke vainly and falsely'; the English turns it into a fresh claim.

fix.find: "I know what I do not know" or "I see what I do not see," and speaks with vanity and falsehood
fix.replace: "Not knowing, I said 'I know'; not seeing, I said 'I see'; I spoke vainly and falsely,"

errors.english: "You have power;
errors.why: The nun says 'I have power (over it)'.

errors.english: seeing each as two-fold makes eight types of knowledge. These are the patience
errors.why: The gloss on 'knowledge' ends with two for each truth; then a new lemma 'seeing' (mthong ba) is glossed as the eight patiences (kṣānti); the English merges the lemma and makes the patiences types of knowledge.

fix.find: seeing each as two-fold makes eight types of knowledge. These are the patience
fix.replace: two for each. "Seeing" refers to the eight: the patience

errors.english: [note: superhuman or superior human states]
errors.why: The commentary glosses 'human dharma' itself as the five hindrances; 'superior' belongs to the next lemma (bla ma), so the note misleads.

note: The word-by-word commentary on the nuns' fourth pārājika is mostly followed, but the confession formula, a first-person claim and the 'seeing' lemma are mishandled.

errors.english: because the sprout is what is produced, the sprout is the agent
errors.why: The sprout is the agent because it is the one that arises (as Devadatta is agent of going), not because it is the thing produced.

note: A faithful rendering of this sub-commentary on the simultaneity objection and the balance-beam example, with one slip in the agent reasoning.

errors.english: Though the (Bodhisattva) Hero of Enlightenment has passed into (nirvana) the state beyond suffering, he still accomplishes all purposes.
errors.why: It is the Jina-pillar, established through the bodhisattva's conduct, that accomplishes all aims even after the bodhisattva has passed into nirvāṇa.

errors.english: Just as a wish-fulfilling jewel or a (kalpavriksha) wishing tree completely fulfills hopes
errors.why: The side is Bodhicaryāvatāra IX verse throughout; the English renders it as prose paragraphs.

note: A faithful rendering of Bodhicaryāvatāra IX on mind-only, illusion and the garuḍa-pillar, prosified, with one misattributed agent.

errors.english: In reply to the claim that contradiction consists precisely in the distinction between a cause that acts after enduring and its effect, the text says: "Fire..."
errors.why: The Tibetan says the reply itself (given by 'Fire...') is that contradiction consists in that qualification of cause and effect; the English makes it the claim being answered.

note: A careful rendering of a dense lemma-by-lemma commentary on fire and cold as contradictories, with one framing inverted.
